Subject: Clarify retention disposition for user requests vs model-generated results

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the call this morning. A couple of BrightBank follow-ups from security/procurement: we need a concise explanation of what Redwood keeps by default for hosted API requests and the corresponding deletion/erasure paths (requests, model outputs, and any derived artifacts). They want text suitable for a procurement questionnaire and a short one‑page summary to attach to the SOW.

Can you confirm the defaults so I can share? Specific asks from them:
- Which elements are stored by default (raw user input, model responses, intermediate artifacts like KV cache entries or embeddings)?
- Default retention horizons for each class (if any defaults apply).
- How customers can shorten/harden retention (e.g., per-request flags, account-level settings, private deployment options).
- The deletion workflow and timeline — what triggers hard deletion vs tombstone/archival retention.

I've attached a quick one-pager (retain_horizon_one-pager.pdf) that I drafted — it's rough. If you can edit or give bullet answers we can send back to Alice today.

Appreciate it,
Jordan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify retention disposition for user requests vs model-generated results

Jordan —

Thanks for the ping and the draft. Below are concise, procurement-friendly bullets you can send straight to BrightBank; I've called out a couple of optional configurations they may care about. I edited the one-pager and added a short summary in-line.

Authoritative defaults (hosted Redwood API):
- Requests (user-provided inputs / prompts): retained by default for 45 days to support abuse detection, model quality monitoring, and ops debugging.
- Model responses (generated outputs): retained by default for 30 days and considered derivative artifacts. These are used for quality monitoring and are subject to the same erasure options below.
- Runtime artifacts (KV cache, ephemeral session state): not persisted beyond the session for standard workloads; short-lived caches are retained only in memory or transient stores and are not part of the retention horizon.
- Embeddings/indexing: persisted only if the customer explicitly requests embedding storage or uses the indexing feature — not stored by default.

Options to shorten or harden retention:
- Account-level setting: we can configure a tenant-level default to reduce capture windows (e.g., set prompts retention to 0 days) — requires signed change order for Hosted customers.
- Per-request flag: customers can set an opt-out header that prevents storing the request/response for model improvement (supported on all tiers).
- Dedicated/Private: Dedicated and Private deployments offer full control — customers can enforce local TTLs or disable telemetry entirely in Private mode.

Deletion & erasure workflow:
- Soft-delete: at policy horizon (e.g., 30/45 days) items are tombstoned and excluded from analytics and model-fine-tuning stores.
- Hard-delete: backend purge jobs run within 48–72 hours of tombstone for standard objects; indices and backups are scrubbed according to the retention schedule and overwrite windows (up to an additional 7 days for some replica cleanup tasks).
- Audit trails: deletion events are logged to an immutable audit stream (accessible under enterprise plans) for compliance reporting.

Attachments/Supporting evidence:
- SOC 2/ISO artifacts are available on request for procurement (we typically share an auditor summary and a redacted control matrix under an NDA).

Suggested send (short): I recommend trimming the one-pager to the bullets above and adding a single callout: “If you require a shorter default retention window we can propose a Dedicated or Private deployment or a Hosted tenant-level configuration; next steps would be an engineering change order and review with security.”

LMK and I’ll finalize the PDF.

-Kim

Kimberly Park

Alice / BrightBank team —

Per our internal review, please find a short summary below and an attached one-page you can include in procurement. Let me know if you want this converted to a table or added to your procurement portal.

Summary (short):
- User inputs (prompts/requests): retained by default for 45 days to support abuse detection and ops debugging. Can be reduced or disabled via a tenant-level setting (requires change order) or per-request opt-out header.
- Model outputs (generated responses): retained by default for 30 days. Also can be excluded via the same opt-out mechanisms.
- Transient runtime artifacts (KV cache/session state): not persisted beyond the active session in standard hosted mode.
- Embeddings/indexes: only stored if explicitly requested by the customer.
- Deletion flow: items are tombstoned at the retention horizon and purged by backend jobs within approximately 48–72 hours; backups/replica cleanup can extend final erasure by up to 7 additional days in rare cases. Audit records of deletion events are available under enterprise agreements.

Attachments: retention_summary_BB.pdf (one-page).

If BrightBank wants a contractual retention horizon (shorter than the hosted default) we can outline the engineering change order and timeline. For regulated workloads we typically recommend Dedicated or Private deployment so you can set and operate your own TTLs.

Best,
Jordan

2) For the 48–72 hour purge window after tombstone, can that be tightened under an enterprise SLA?

If you can pass those to Kim or engineering that would be helpful. Otherwise we’re comfortable moving forward to the next procurement step.

Appreciate it —
Alice
